reasons: Both give the same correct NOT EXISTS anti-join with a relative 90-day window, only the given columns, and the never-ordered caveat, so all four rubric items are met on each side. A edges ahead on accuracy and honest uncertainty: it marks its index claim as a structural expectation and tells the user to run EXPLAIN ANALYZE, warns against a redundant index, and adds a deterministic ORDER BY, whereas B asserts that LEFT JOIN ... IS NULL forces the whole join before filtering, which is wrong for the PostgreSQL dialect it names. B's concision and in-block dialect comment are real advantages, which is why the margin is small rather than clear.

B: Claims LEFT JOIN ... IS NULL 'forces the whole join before filtering'; PostgreSQL's planner recognises that pattern and executes it as an anti-join, so it is not generally forced to materialise the full join first.
